# dlargv

> Generates a vector of real plane rotations (Givens rotations).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlargv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlargv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlargv( N, x, strideX, y, strideY, c, strideC ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of plane rotations to generate |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output vector x |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `x` |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incy</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output vector y |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride for `y` |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incc</sub> | **out** · Output vector for cosines |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride for `c` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of plane rotations to be generated.
- `x`: dimension (1+(N-1)\*`INCX`) On entry, the vector x. On exit, x(i) is overwritten by a(i), for $i = 1$,...,n.
- `y`: dimension (1+(N-1)\*`INCY`) On entry, the vector y. On exit, the sines of the plane rotations.
- `c`: The cosines of the plane rotations.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlargv.ndarray(
    N,
    x, strideX, offsetX,
    y, strideY, offsetY,
    c, strideC, offsetC
) → Float64Array
```

Generates a vector of real plane rotations (Givens rotations).

For `i = 0, 1, ..., N-1`:

```text
  (  c(i)  s(i) ) ( x(i) ) = ( a(i) )
  ( -s(i)  c(i) ) ( y(i) ) = (   0  )
```

On exit, `x` is overwritten by `a`, `y` is overwritten by the sines,
and `c` receives the cosines of the plane rotations.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of plane rotations to generate |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output vector x |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incy</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output vector y |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride for `y` |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incc</sub> | **out** · Output vector for cosines |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride for `c` |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `c` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of plane rotations to be generated.
- `x`: dimension (1+(N-1)\*`INCX`) On entry, the vector x. On exit, x(i) is overwritten by a(i), for $i = 1$,...,n.
- `y`: dimension (1+(N-1)\*`INCY`) On entry, the vector y. On exit, the sines of the plane rotations.
- `c`: The cosines of the plane rotations.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dlargv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlargv';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const x = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const y = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const c = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dlargv( N, x, 1, y, 1, c, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dlargv.ndarray( N, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0, c, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLARGV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLARGV generates a vector of real plane rotations, determined by elements of the real vectors x and y. For $i = 1$,2,...,n

```text
(  c(i)  s(i) ) ( x(i) ) = ( a(i) )
( -s(i)  c(i) ) ( y(i) ) = (   0  )
```

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
